src/report.c

The report writer reads recorded outcomes and timings. It computes rankings from those records; no algorithm name is preselected as the winner.

Format counts and escape diagnostic strings

Section titled “Format counts and escape diagnostic strings”

Helpers calculate rates, classify outcomes and identify wrong targets. CSV strings double embedded quotes so names cannot change the number of columns. FNV-1a fingerprints identify manifests; they are reproducibility checks, not cryptographic authenticity checks. The ranking compares dangerous errors, then recovered typos, then measured latency.

Weighted mode checks cost first. */78static int better(size_t algorithm, size_t b, const Evaluation *evaluations, Costs cost, int weighted) {79    const Metrics *left = &evaluations[algorithm].metrics, *right = &evaluations[b].metrics;80    if (weighted && metric_cost(left, cost) != metric_cost(right, cost)) return metric_cost(left, cost) < metric_cost(right,81        cost);82    if (danger(left) != danger(right)) return danger(left) < danger(right);83    if (left->fuzzy != right->fuzzy) return left->fuzzy > right->fuzzy;84    return evaluations[algorithm].perf[0].end.median_ns < evaluations[b].perf[0].end.median_ns;85}8687typedef struct {88    size_t algorithm;89    unsigned dangerous, recovered;90    double latency;91} RankedAlgorithm;9293/** Carry comparison keys with each row; C99 qsort needs no global context. */94static int compare_rank(const void *left, const void *right) {95    const RankedAlgorithm *a = left, *b = right;96    if (a->dangerous != b->dangerous) return (a->dangerous > b->dangerous) ? 1 : -1;97    if (a->recovered != b->recovered) return (a->recovered < b->recovered) ? 1 : -1;98    if (a->latency != b->latency) return (a->latency > b->latency) ? 1 : -1;99    return (a->algorithm > b->algorithm) - (a->algorithm < b->algorithm);100}101

Write every case and its selected policy to CSV

Section titled “Write every case and its selected policy to CSV”

One row includes the input, intended outcome, chosen status, top two suggestions and scores. Missing intended scores use -1. Summary and runtime CSVs are written from the same evaluation structures. Every stream is checked for write and close failures.

Render the twelve report sections from measured data

Section titled “Render the twelve report sections from measured data”

Section writers explain counts, timing, collisions, failures, threshold sensitivity and limits. Category rows use the same counters as aggregate results. Safety conclusions remain limited to these labels and policies. qsort workspace is identified as library-dependent instead of being hidden in a claimed stack-only bound.

"576        "Recalibrate on representative development data when the schema or typo population "577        "changes, then evaluate on a fresh untouched hold-out. For unit, security or "578        "destructive settings, consider suggestion-only correction or an explicit confirmation "579        "step before applying a fuzzy match. Reject duplicate resolved names, invalid "580        "values, normalization collisions and missing required values.\n\n## 12. Limitations "581        "and future improvements\n\nThis is a finite, partly generated English/ASCII "582        "dataset. Calibration uses disjoint vocabulary and may transfer poorly; mutation "583        "patterns still overlap by design. The five already-correct original examples "584        "are in the formatting group; the five misspelled originals are in the deletion "585        "group. The ambiguity group includes formatting variants of ten semantic phrases "586        "and therefore has fewer independent semantic families than raw cases. Safety "587        "outcomes depend on these application-defined labels. No aliases or value-aware "588        "rules are evaluated.\n\nShort identifiers and 128-byte near-identical names "589        "stress policies trained mostly on longer calibration names. Threshold grids "590        "are finite and might miss useful operating points. Exact normalization cannot "591        "detect a user's semantic mistake that spells another canonical name correctly. "592        "Digits have higher cost only in the documented weighted variant; other methods "593        "treat them like letters. Unicode, locale-sensitive case folding, sections, "594        "escaping and full INI syntax are outside this baseline.\n\nTiming uses one "595        "shared host, a small probe set and finite repetitions; OS scheduling, CPU frequency "596        "and timer overhead add variance. Latency distributions are descriptive; tail "597        "estimates from a small sample are especially unstable. No real-application "598        "1000-property accuracy claim follows from synthetic scaling tests. Workspace "599        "values are source-derived bounds, not observed RSS. Further work should add "600        "independently authored schemas, naturally occurring errors, family-aware resampling, "601        "more process-level timing repetitions, allocation/RSS instrumentation, optional "602        "reviewed aliases and deployment-specific severity weights.\n\n## Reproduction "603        "and evidence\n\nRun `make`, `make test`, `make sanitize`, then `make benchmark` "604        "from the project directory. The default manifests use seed 42. For another "605        "seed run `./property_match_bench --generate --seed N`, then `./property_match_bench "606        "--benchmark --seed N`; this explicitly replaces the manifests. Preserve them "607        "with the report. `--wrong-cost` and `--reject-cost` change policy selection "608        "and weighted rankings.\n\nThe baseline and every fuzzy method are evaluated "609        "on identical held-out inputs. `reports/results.csv` (or the supplied --csv "610        "path) contains individual classifications, thresholds and suggestions; `reports/summary.csv` "611        "contains aggregate counts; `reports/runtime.csv` contains timing data; and "612        "`reports/calibration_grid.csv` contains calibration evidence. The benchmark "613        "aborts if correctness tests or dataset validation fail, preventing invalid "614        "implementations from entering rankings.\n",615        file);616}

Select rankings and assemble the report after measurement

Section titled “Select rankings and assemble the report after measurement”

The final function selects safety, weighted-cost and performance recommendations, then invokes section writers. POSIX gmtime_r writes UTC into a caller-owned struct tm; banned gmtime is absent. A C99-only platform without a permitted reentrant converter reports the timestamp unavailable. No report work is inside the matching timer.

Reference for the contracts used in this file

Section titled “Reference for the contracts used in this file”

The benchmark methodology defines each denominator and ranking rule. The report renders stored outcomes; it does not choose new thresholds from held-out errors. Open reference.

617/** Build CSV evidence first, then assemble Markdown from the same records. */618int generate_report(const Options *options, const Dataset *calibration, const Dataset *held_out, const Evaluation *evaluations) {619    FILE *file;620    size_t algorithm, rank[ALGORITHMS - 1], best = 1, balanced = 1, fast = ALGORITHMS;621    RankedAlgorithm ranked[ALGORITHMS - 1];622    unsigned min_danger = ~0U;623    time_t stamp = time(NULL);624    struct tm utc;625    int have_utc = 0;626#if defined(__unix__) || defined(__APPLE__)627    have_utc = gmtime_r(&stamp, &utc) != NULL;628#else629    (void)stamp; /* C99 has no reentrant UTC converter permitted by banned.h. */630#endif631    char timestamp[64];632    if (!write_csv(options, held_out, evaluations)) return 0;633    file = fopen(options->report, "w");634    if (!file) return 0;635    if (have_utc) strftime(timestamp, sizeof timestamp, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", &utc);636    else memcpy(timestamp, "unavailable", strlen("unavailable") + 1);637    for (algorithm = 1; algorithm < ALGORITHMS; ++algorithm) {638        if (better(algorithm, best, evaluations, options->costs, 0)) best = algorithm;639        if (better(algorithm, balanced, evaluations, options->costs, 1)) balanced = algorithm;640        if (danger(&evaluations[algorithm].metrics) < min_danger) min_danger = danger(&evaluations[algorithm].metrics);641        ranked[algorithm - 1] = (RankedAlgorithm){algorithm, danger(&evaluations[algorithm].metrics),642            evaluations[algorithm].metrics.fuzzy, evaluations[algorithm].perf[0].end.median_ns};643    }644    for (algorithm = 1; algorithm < ALGORITHMS; ++algorithm) {645        int meets_safety_requirement = danger(&evaluations[algorithm].metrics) == min_danger;646        int recovers_at_least_one_typo = evaluations[algorithm].metrics.fuzzy != 0;647        int faster_than_current = fast == ALGORITHMS ||648            evaluations[algorithm].perf[0].end.median_ns < evaluations[fast].perf[0].end.median_ns;649        if (meets_safety_requirement && recovers_at_least_one_typo && faster_than_current) fast = algorithm;650    }651    /* Sort small records containing comparison keys;
